s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with motor and speech impairment
salient_findings: Episodes of spasms and tremors in the right hand and forearm
key_facts: Woman in her mid-60s
Initial carpal tunnel release surgery
Recurring tremors
Referred to a neurologist 7 months later
Developed progressive right-sided weakness over 3 months
Brain MRI showed hyperintensities in bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter and other areas
No contrast enhancement on T1-weighted MRI
Brain biopsy showed CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ cells
Cerebrospinal fluid contained lymphoma cells
Bone marrow was negative for lymphoma cells

shortlist.why_kept: Brain MRI showed hyperintensities in bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter and other areas

shortlist.why_kept: Progressive right-sided weakness, dysarthria, and gait instability

rule_in.why: age and sex are not distinctive

rule_out.why: age and sex are not specific

trace.fact: Chief complaint: episodes of spasms and tremors in her right hand and forearm

rule_in.why: it often presents with focal neurological symptoms

rule_out.why: the fact is compatible with multiple neurological conditions

trace.fact: Initial treatment: carpal tunnel release surgery

rule_in.why: surgery is unrelated to the candidates

rule_out.why: surgery is unrelated to neurological conditions

trace.fact: Progression of symptoms: over the subsequent 3 months

rule_in.why: it is characterized by progressive worsening

rule_out.why: it typically has a monophasic course

trace.fact: Symptom progression: developed progressive right-sided weakness

rule_in.why: it often presents with progressive unilateral weakness

rule_out.why: it typically presents with asymmetric apraxia and rigidity rather than progressive weakness
dysarthria is less typical in early stages
hand tremors are compatible with all candidates
